task.description:
RE-VALIDATION after your own Step 2d FAIL on OQ-5 (this exact handoff file, previous result below is your own prior FAIL verdict -- read it first for full context, then verify the rework actually resolves it rather than re-deriving OQ-5 from scratch). Your prior ruling: M6's insert-if-absent creation of an instance_projections row oversteps into EE-01/S3's deferred 'meaningful population at instance-start' territory; required CODE-DESIGNER to redesign M1's 'no row found' branch and M6's create-vs-update split, then ELIXIR-DEV to re-implement, before this gate re-runs. Both happened: design doc reworked and independently re-validated (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASS, step-01b handoff -- M1 now fails with {:error, :instance_not_started} on no row, M6 is update-only via InstanceProjection.update_changeset/2, §9 OQ-5 marked RESOLVED); ELIXIR-DEV re-implemented per that design (commit aac8f256, step-02a handoff PASS); SECURITY-REVIEWER re-ran the full INV-1..INV-8 gate against the new code (step-02c handoff, 4th pass, PASS -- specifically re-verified update_changeset/2 can't cast tenant_id and the new changes-map pattern-match in update_projection/3 can't crash given Ecto.Multi's short-circuit ordering).

Your job now: (1) Confirm OQ-5 is genuinely resolved, not just relabeled -- read the CURRENT lib/letflow/event_store.ex (git diff main...HEAD) and lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md's current §6.2.1/§6.2.6/§9 yourself, don't trust any agent's self-report. Specifically verify M6 (update_projection/3) contains zero create/insert/upsert path for instance_projections -- it should be a bare repo.update/2 via InstanceProjection.update_changeset/2, nothing else. (2) Re-run your standard idiom review (idiomatic vs. crutch, supervision, type-safety gaps, scope creep) fresh against the CURRENT diff (not just the OQ-5-relevant hunk -- confirm nothing else drifted since your last review, e.g. the moduledoc/comment updates ELIXIR-DEV made). (3) Re-check docs/anti-patterns.md. (4) Confirm the is_struct/1 INV-8 guard pattern you previously confirmed consistent is still intact and untouched by this latest change (it should be -- M1/M6 are unrelated code paths -- but verify, don't assume).
acceptance_criteria: idiomatic-vs-crutch, supervision, type-safety-gap, and scope-creep questions all explicitly answered
OQ-5 (instance_projections insert-if-absent scope question) explicitly confirmed or rejected, with reasoning, not silently passed through

result.summary:
RE-VALIDATION of my own prior Step 2d FAIL (OQ-5). Read the current lib/letflow/event_store.ex in full (git diff main...HEAD, 582 lines, new file), the current lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md §6.2.1 (M1), §6.2.6 (M6), and §9 OQ-5, lib/letflow/event_store/instance_projection.ex's insert_changeset/2 and update_changeset/2, lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex's diff, and docs/anti-patterns.md. Did not trust any prior agent's self-report -- re-derived each finding from the current source.

JOB 1 -- OQ-5 confirmed genuinely resolved, not relabeled.

active_instance_guard/3 (M1, event_store.ex ~line 320): `repo.get(InstanceProjection, instance_id, prefix: schema_name)` -- on `nil` returns `{:error, :instance_not_started}`, a case DISTINCT from `{:error, {:instance_terminated, status}}`. No insert, no upsert, no default-row construction anywhere in this function. On a found non-terminal row, returns `{:ok, projection}` (the real struct, not a bare atom) so M6 can reuse it without a second read.

update_projection/3 (M6, event_store.ex ~line 555): takes `active_instance_guard: %InstanceProjection{} = projection` from Multi's changes map (a hard pattern-match -- if M1 hadn't already produced a struct, this step would never even be reached, since Multi short-circuits on M1's error first), builds `attrs = %{status: projection.status, last_event_seq: assigned_sequence_number}` (status passed through unchanged, never derived from attrs/caller input), and calls `projection |> InstanceProjection.update_changeset(attrs) |> repo.update(prefix: schema_name)`. Confirmed by reading instance_projection.ex directly: `update_changeset/2` is `cast(attrs, [:status, :last_event_seq]) |> validate_required(...) |> validate_number(...)` -- `:instance_id` and `:tenant_id` are structurally absent from its cast list (moduledoc states this explicitly: 'instance_id and tenant_id are structurally not castable here'), so even a corrupted attrs map could not smuggle a create-shaped write through this changeset. Grepped the whole module for `insert_changeset`, `on_conflict`, and `Multi.insert` in the vicinity of InstanceProjection: the only two hits are M1's read-only `repo.get` and M6's `repo.update` -- zero create/insert/upsert path for instance_projections anywhere in this file. `insert_changeset/2` exists on the schema module but is never referenced from event_store.ex.

Design doc cross-check: §6.2.1 states M1's no-row case is 'update-only per REVIEWER's Step 2d OQ-5 ruling: append/2 never originates an instance_projections row'; §6.2.6 states M6 'therefore uses InstanceProjection.update_changeset/2 -- never insert_changeset/2 and never an on_conflict:-based upsert'; §9 OQ-5 is explicitly marked 'RESOLVED per REVIEWER's Step 2d ruling ... no longer open' with the full reasoning restated accurately (matches my own prior FAIL verdict's reasoning, not a watered-down paraphrase); §11's acceptance-criteria traceability table adds an explicit note that every AC1-AC6 test must pre-seed instance_projections via direct Repo.insert in test setup, which is the correct consequence of this ruling and hands TEST-DESIGNER an unambiguous fixture strategy. OQ-5: CONFIRMED RESOLVED.

JOB 2 -- fresh idiom review against the CURRENT full diff (not just the OQ-5 hunk):
(1) Idiomatic vs. crutch -- unchanged from my prior review and still holds: Ecto.Multi composition is idiomatic (one Multi.run/3 per named step, changes-map threading used correctly, on_conflict:/conflict_target: for the two real upserts that remain -- M2 instance_sequence and M3 idempotency -- Ecto's lock("FOR UPDATE") query composition for the row lock per INV-7, not a raw SQL string). M1/M6's rework replaced what was previously a crutch-adjacent upsert-as-create-path with the idiomatic alternative (a hard pattern-match on an already-fetched struct plus a real update changeset) -- this is a straightforward improvement, not a new crutch introduced to satisfy the gate. No hand-rolled retry loops, no racy check-then-write patterns anywhere in the current diff.
(2) Supervision -- N/A, confirmed again. Both changed modules (Letflow.EventStore, Letflow.TenantProvisioning) remain plain context modules: no use GenServer/Supervisor/gen_statem, no spawn, no process registration, nothing touching Letflow.InstanceSupervisor. The M1/M6 rework touches only ordinary function bodies, no process/supervision surface introduced or removed.
(3) Type-safety gaps (noted, not blocking, same class as before): (a) M6's pattern-match `%{active_instance_guard: %InstanceProjection{} = projection}` is a runtime guarantee resting on Multi's step ordering and SECURITY-REVIEWER's re-verified short-circuit semantics, not something the type system enforces -- a future refactor that reorders build_multi/1's pipeline (e.g. moving update_projection before active_instance_guard) would fail this match at runtime with a MatchError inside Multi.run/3's closure rather than being caught at compile time; a stricter type system with dependent/session-typed step ordering would catch this, Elixir cannot. This is an accepted, reasoned tradeoff (documented in the M6 comment block), not an oversight, but worth naming per the task's standing 'note it even if not asked' instruction. (b) interpret_transaction_result/1's catch-all clause (unchanged from prior review) still silently routes any future 7th Multi step's untyped error through the generic {:error, reason} branch rather than forcing an exhaustiveness check -- same finding as before, still applies, still just a watch item. (c) update_changeset/2's `cast(attrs, [:status, :last_event_seq])` relies on M6 always passing `status: projection.status` (read-back, not caller-derived) to avoid ever actually changing status via an ordinary append -- correct today, but nothing at the type level stops a future edit from passing a different status value through this same changeset; the boundary that keeps status EE-01/S3-owned is a code-review convention (this very gate), not a compile-time or schema-level constraint. Worth flagging as the kind of boundary a sum type or a separate status-transition-only changeset would enforce structurally.
(4) Scope creep -- the M1/M6 rework is a net REDUCTION in scope relative to the version I FAILed: it removes the insert/upsert path entirely rather than adding new abstraction. No new behaviours, macros, or generic plumbing appear anywhere in the current diff. tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 (tenant_provisioning.ex) is unchanged since my prior review and remains a narrowly-scoped pure function required by the settled 0003 addendum. No new scope-creep findings.

Moduledoc/comment drift check (explicitly requested): the event_store.ex moduledoc's 'Scope' section now states the OQ-5 outcome directly ('append/2 never originates an instance_projections row ... A missing row fails the whole call with {:error, :instance_not_started} instead') -- this is new text since my last review but it accurately restates the ruling, not a reinterpretation of it. All other moduledoc sections (tenant_id derivation, event_id/created_at single-mint, pre-transaction validation timing, instance_sequence/event_idempotency's missing tenant_id column) are byte-for-byte consistent with what I reviewed previously. No other drift found.

JOB 3 -- docs/anti-patterns.md re-checked in full (122 lines, 3 entries: Docker toolchain workaround, requirement_status.yaml overwrite, handoff timestamp estimation). None apply to this diff -- confirmed again, nothing new to log.

JOB 4 -- INV-8 is_struct/1 guard re-verified intact and untouched. Grepped event_store.ex: the guard `defp validate_metadata(metadata) when not is_map(metadata) or is_struct(metadata) do` at line 259 is byte-identical to what I reviewed in the prior pass, in the same single location, unchanged by the M1/M6 rework (confirmed these are non-overlapping code regions -- validate_metadata/1 is part of the pre-transaction phase, P0-P6; M1/M6 are Multi steps in the transactional phase, §6.2). No second guard needed or introduced elsewhere.

Toolchain/compile check: mix compile ran clean against the current branch (exit 0, zero warnings/errors) -- this environment does have a working Elixir/mix toolchain (Erlang/OTP 27, Mix 1.18.3), so this is a real compile confirmation, not a 'can't verify' fallback.

Overall verdict: PASS. OQ-5 is genuinely resolved at the code level (verified independently against instance_projection.ex's actual cast lists, not just the design doc's prose) and at the design level (§9 correctly marked RESOLVED with accurate reasoning). No new blocking findings. Three non-blocking type-safety watch items noted per the standing instruction to report them even unprompted (7b runtime pattern-match on Multi step ordering; catch-all error routing not exhaustive-checked; status-passthrough boundary enforced by convention not by type). Route to TEST-DESIGNER.
